claims.text: Surface oxidation-state distribution is a key determinant of catalytic activity in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Increasing the relative Pt fraction will reduce surface oxide formation.
Pt is a comparatively oxidation-resistant component under the proposed ethanol-oxidation conditions.
Reduced oxide formation preserves a larger fraction of active metallic surface sites.
The preserved metallic sites facilitate ethanol adsorption and oxidation.
The baseline is an equimolar nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalyst.
The baseline catalyst has a heterogeneous distribution of surface oxidation states under operating conditions.
The controlled intervention is an approximately 5–10% increase in Pt content relative to the equimolar baseline.
Pt enrichment will reduce oxidation specifically at Pt surface sites.
Increasing Pt content will reduce the formation of strongly bound oxygen species during ethanol oxidation.
A larger fraction of metallic sites will enhance the adsorption and activation of ethanol molecules.
The Pt-enriched catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential than the equimolar baseline.
The Pt-enriched catalyst will produce higher current densities than the equimolar baseline.
The proposed effect is limited to typical electrochemical ethanol-oxidation potential windows and electrolyte systems and may not transfer to other reactions or drastically different conditions.
Surface restructuring and changes in reaction intermediates may compete with the proposed Pt-enrichment effect.

Failure to observe both a statistically significant decrease in onset potential and an increase in current density, or failure to observe reduced Pt-site oxidation, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
